context: After the upstream skill and diagnostic changes land, define a BenchBox authority model and stable policy IDs, reduce AGENTS.md to concise cross-agent project policy, keep agent adapters thin, move operational detail to durable runbooks, repair executable Claude surfaces, and add a deterministic audit plus scenario corpus. Capture baseline and post-change effectiveness, efficiency, and conformance metrics, and wire the guard and required CI in the same PR.
description: BenchBox agent policy is large, duplicated, and weakly evaluated. AGENTS.md is roughly 425 lines and 19 KB; CLAUDE.md is a pointer rather than a native import; GEMINI.md and ANTIGRAVITY.md substantially duplicate policy; the Claude /pr command can add an unconditional Claude coauthor and has ambiguous dirty-worktree commit behavior; project hooks duplicate global hooks, invoke bare python3, mutate edits, and swallow failures; and no rule requires agents to identify the authority behind words such as required. The earlier required Claude author incident was task-local, not repository policy, and exposed this provenance gap.

anti_patterns.dont: Build a structured-policy generator before the concise documents and checks prove it necessary
anti_patterns.instead: Use Markdown, stable policy IDs, and small deterministic checks
anti_patterns.why: A new abstraction would add maintenance cost before the policy model is validated

anti_patterns.dont: Duplicate AGENTS.md into a Copilot-specific file without loader evidence
anti_patterns.instead: Use AGENTS.md when the consumer supports it

anti_patterns.dont: Edit generated skill mirrors as the source of truth
anti_patterns.instead: Change canonical skills upstream and regenerate through skill-sync
anti_patterns.why: They will drift from canonical skills and be overwritten

anti_patterns.dont: Land the audit without required-CI wiring
anti_patterns.instead: Land the guard and path-filtered required check together

preserves.behavior: BenchBox worktree isolation, uv-only Python execution, explicit staging, and protected-branch safety remain normative
No agent identity is imposed unless the current authorized task explicitly requires it
Review authorization stays read-only until implementation is explicitly requested
Soundness-path auto-merge exceptions and existing release safety remain intact
The audit and its required-CI wiring land in the same PR
